etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French prompt, from Latin prōmptus (“visible, apparent, evident”), past participle of prōmō (“to take or bring out or forth, produce, bring to light”), from prō (“forth, forward”) + emō (“to take, acquire, buy”).

quote.citation: 1623, William Shakespeare, Antony & Cleopatra, act 3, scene 8:
quote.text: Tell him, I am prompt / To lay my Crowne at's feete, and there to kneele.

definitions.definition: (finance) Front: closest or nearest, in futures trading.

quote.citation: 2013 July 5, Davis W. Edwards, Energy Investing DeMystified: A Self-Teaching Guide, McGraw Hill Professional, →ISBN, page 19:
quote.text: When physical crude oil transactions are priced, they are usually marked to the prompt month futures contract. The prompt month futures contract is the next futures contract to settle.

quote.citation: 2021 May 11, Neil C. Schofield, Commodity Derivatives: Markets and Applications, John Wiley & Sons, →ISBN, page 448:
quote.text: The settlement ratio is determined as follows: i) If the prompt futures price of coal at maturity is less than or equal to the floor price, the ratio will be one.

definitions.definition: (writing) A suggestion for inspiration given to an author.
(business, dated) A time limit given for payment of an account for produce purchased, this limit varying with different goods.

quote.citation: 1848, John Stuart Mill, Principles of Political Economy: With Some of Their Applications to Social Philosophy. […], volume (please specify |volume=I or II), London: John W[illiam] Parker, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: To cover any probable difference of price which might arise before the expiration of the prompt, which for this article [tea] is three months.

definitions.definition: (computing) A sequence of characters that is displayed to indicate that a computer is ready to receive input.
(machine learning) Textual input given to a large language model or image model in order to have it generate a desired output.

quote.citation: 2022 April 15, Steven Johnson, Nikita Iziev, “A.I. Is Mastering Language. Should We Trust What It Says?”, in The New York Times‎[1], →ISSN:
quote.text: For instance, using the “instruct” mode, I once gave GPT-3 the prompt: “Write an essay discussing the role of metafiction in the work of Italo Calvino.”

definitions.definition: (transitive) To lead (someone) toward what they should say or do.
(transitive) To say (something) in order to help or encourage someone to speak.

quote.citation: 1988, Tad Williams, chapter 5, in The Dragonbone Chair, DAW Books, →ISBN:
quote.text: "What is your name, you?" he demanded. The captured youth tried to pull free again, but was obviously tiring. After a moment he stopped his struggling altogether. "Your name?" Simon prompted, this time in a softer tone."Malachias." The youth turned away panting.

quote.citation: 2007 December, Margaret Mayo, Helen Brooks, Carole Mortimer, A Presents Christmas Bundle: An Anthology, Harlequin, page 51:
quote.text: ‘Be warned, Molly,’ Gideon added harshly. ‘I won't ever let you do or say anything that will hurt Crys. Is that understood?’ he prompted determinedly.

definitions.definition: (transitive, theater and television) To show or tell (an actor/person) the words they should be saying, or actions they should be doing.
(transitive) To initiate; to cause or lead to.

quote.citation: 1996, Tad Williams, chapter 7, in City of Golden Shadow, Legend Books, →ISBN:
quote.text: At first Renie's chain of thought had been prompted by the unsatisfactory nature of phone contact compared to an actual meeting, […]

quote.citation: 2011 September 2, Phil McNulty, “Bulgaria 0-3 England”, in BBC‎[2]:
quote.text: The only sour note on a virtually perfect night for England came from shameful 'monkey' chanting aimed at Ashley Cole and Ashley Young from a section of Bulgaria's fans which later prompted an official complaint from the Football Association to Uefa.

quote.citation: 2012, Christoper Zara, Tortured Artists: From Picasso and Monroe to Warhol and Winehouse, the Twisted Secrets of the World's Most Creative Minds, part 1, chapter 1, 27:
quote.text: On October 6, 1927, Warner Bros. released The Jazz Singer, the first sound-synched feature film, prompting a technological shift of unprecedented speed and unstoppable force. Within two years, nearly every studio release was a talkie.

definitions.definition: (transitive, computing) To request (a user) to provide input or do something on a computer.
(transitive, machine learning) To provide textual input in the form of ordinary language to (an artificial intelligence or language model) to have it generate a desired output.
